# Independent audit: oriented and fiber-labeled cap pyramids

Full read of `candidate 600f7b09ccd06ced` and `candidate aee564c922d3f5fe`: **PASS, no repair identified.** This audit concerns the geometric proofs, normalizations and limiting scope; it does not infer the theorems from a numerical screen.

For the single-body note, the actual cap contains the pyramid over its complete cut section with any farthest captured apex. Its height is h_(B-g)(u) for a unit cap normal, so volume is s h/d. The average cap volume is beta|B| because the cut planes pass through g and their divergence contribution is zero; the old boundary divergence weight is exactly the normal-only support value h_(B-g)(n), permitting use of the stated normal marginal. The direction in V_1(-J,B), and the order with J repeated d-1 times, are correct. Every nonnegative remainder is actual cap excess, and equality forces every positive-weight cap to equal its contained pyramid. The complement gives an upper bound for beta, not another lower bound. The simplex factor d and the cube value 1/(2d) check directly.

For the labeled note, allocated T is coarea, hence the directed cone term is [h(u)-tau]T with no extra |u|. At an inside supporting facet, the allocated base density is at most one and bounds a weighted pyramid. At an outside facet its height and volume are zero regardless of allocation. Strict full fibers correctly remain entirely in the remainder. These statements also hold for interval endpoint counting.

Expanding tau=c-a.z independently gives

    sum_z [h_z(u)-c+a.z]T_z
      =sum_z h_z(u)T_z+a.b_H-delta_H T_H-T_H u.y.

Thus the printed cancellation needs the base mean cap by cap, the through-mark condition, and the weighted continuous balance. A common FULL allocated section mean supplies the first two, even when that mean is only the shared contact barycenter. A group-averaged base mean alone is insufficient. The note keeps this distinction explicitly.

Compatibility gives sum_z T_z h_z(u)<=T h_p(u), so the support deficit is subtracted in the exact cap-volume identity. The (1,2,1) box family checks that the sign matters: its actual Q=2, mixed cone term2, own term3, deficit1 and remainder2d-2 satisfy 2d=3-1+(2d-2). The final three-identical-cube allocation family also checks: the two endpoint sections carry the same gamma, their full mean is zero, and the cone term is 1/2+gamma. Those are consistent inside/outside selectors, not independently assigned areas.

Finally, the compactification uses one joint record/section measure. Uniform support-function convergence and bounded nonzero continuous normals make the entire directed height integrand continuous and bounded; cap volumes converge because their hyperplanes have zero d-volume. The trace clamp is used only where it preserves thresholds and section data. No projected base-normal cover is inferred, and no unbounded product of separately convergent factors is passed. This is the correct scope for the common-section-mean cancellation.

Both notes retain the nonnegative remainder and the unfavorable compatibility deficit. Neither claims a parity payment or substitutes cap volume for first-variation loss.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
